_purpose: Prove the §5.2 post-conversion verification assertion actually FAILS on a genuine continueErrorOutput swallow-node whose main[1] is unwired, when that node 401s. [[green-that-cannot-fail]]: an assertion only ever shown to PASS is not an instrument.
_plan: plans/crm-auth-unification-plan.md §5.2 (dynamic per-node proof), §2 CORRECTION 3 (silent swallow-node failure mode)
_target: CLONE ONLY txiPzSxy3Pclsz6v (sorento-consume-main TEST). Live spine 9qVyfUxmRQqrpGRMDLRuz NOT touched.

chosen_node.name: get-access-types
chosen_node.why_check_access_http_rejected: On the clone check-access-http has onError=null (stopWorkflow) and only main[0] wired -> NOT a swallow-node. The clone splits the live spine's single check-access HTTP node into check-access-http (real call, stopWorkflow) + check-access (code). So the spine's canonical swallow node maps to a non-swallow node on the clone.

swallow_node_proof.main1_error_output: ABSENT from connections -> error output wired to NOTHING
swallow_node_proof.verdict: GENUINE swallow-node: continueErrorOutput AND main[1] unwired

chosen_node.other_genuine_swallow_node_on_clone: get-presigned-url (continueErrorOutput, main[0]->Loop Over Items1, main[1] unwired). Not chosen: only reachable downstream of a real get-results MCP read; get-access-types is reachable by the deterministic AUTH-A7 turn (no LLM, no MCP).
chosen_node.reachability: Bad-CREDENTIAL (not bad contact-id) isolates the 401 to get-access-types alone; upstream check-access-http keeps its valid crm-n8n-auth binding so the AUTH-A7 path (intent_hint=check_promotion) still routes into get-access-types. This closes the plan's §5.2 OPEN GAP (a bad contact-id could never fail get-access-types without also flipping check-access to a legit denial).

credential_binding.rebind_method: REST PUT (MCP cannot bind httpHeaderAuth, LESSONS 55). Body = {name,nodes,connections,settings} from a fresh REST GET, settings.binaryMode stripped (400-trap), ONLY get-access-types.credentials.httpHeaderAuth changed. PUT auto-publishes the clone (accepted).
credential_binding.collateral_after_each_put: 28/28 credential-bearing nodes survived every PUT; only get-access-types binding changed; zero bindings lost; pinData/staticData preserved.

good_run.downstream_reply: Please specify which access level you'd like to use for promotions: (7 access levels offered)

failing_run.http_outcome: 401 Invalid API key. Node RETRIED (retryOnFail=true, executionTime 2282ms) then completed with executionStatus=success -- the 401 did NOT fail the node or the execution.

where_the_401_landed.main1_error_output_UNWIRED: carries the AxiosError envelope {allowed,decision,agent_name, error:{message:'401 - Invalid API key', name:'AxiosError', status:401}} -> routed to the unwired error output -> SWALLOWED, goes nowhere
where_the_401_landed.main0_regular_output_to_Aggregate: carries an EMPTY item {"json":{}} -- NOT the access-types data
where_the_401_landed.actual_consequence: The empty {} on main[0] propagated downstream: Aggregate -> {"name":[]} (hint: 'field name not found') -> access-level-choice-message -> 'You have no access levels configured to get promotions.' A CONFIDENTLY WRONG customer-facing reply, with the whole execution reporting success. This is WORSE than the plan's assumed silent dead-end (no reply).

s52_assertion.which_clause_fired: clause 1 (domain key present in main[0][0].json) -- exactly the clause plan §5.2 predicts is 'the only one that fires'

decorative_clauses_on_bad_run.execution_status==success: PASS (decorative -- would wave the failure through)
decorative_clauses_on_bad_run.node_runData.error==null/absent: PASS (decorative -- would wave it through; the error is inside main[1][0].json.error, not the node-level error field)
decorative_clauses_on_bad_run.search_executions status:error: MISSES it entirely -- 0 error executions; a status-filter reviewer sees nothing
decorative_clauses_on_bad_run.note_main1_empty_clause: For continueErrorOutput, main[1] is NON-empty on failure (holds the error), so that particular decorative clause would incidentally catch it -- but that is mechanism-dependent and NOT the assertion the plan relies on. The load-bearing clause remains main[0][0].json domain-key presence.

downstream_reply.good: Please specify which access level you'd like to use for promotions (7 levels)
downstream_reply.bad: You have no access levels configured to get promotions.

restore.method: REST PUT of the pre-experiment node set (byte-identical restore)
restore.assert_auth_sh: RESULT: PASS (10/10 CRM nodes G1-G4, G5/G5b/G6 all PASS, no residual x-api-key)

egress_safety.both_runs: Zero real egress. All replies emitted as egress-log records (save-message-redis would_log, save-session-vars would_write). get-access-types is a prod READ (permitted); a 401 on a read produces no egress. No sendmsg, no assign, no prod write.
egress_safety.note: The bad run's save-session-vars would_write carried the WRONG 'no access levels' response -- but as a would_write egress-log record, never a real CRM PUT.

verdict: YES -- the §5.2 detector CATCHES the silent swallow-node failure. On a genuine continueErrorOutput node with an unwired main[1], a real 401 leaves main[0][0].json without its domain-specific key (empty {} here), so the assertion's clause-1 comes out FALSE = FAIL, while execution-status and node-level-error checks all decoratively PASS. The instrument has now been shown to FAIL on a real fault, not only to PASS.
